title: Elon Musk's five-step algorithm: why manufacturing beats design (Starbase tour, Part 1)
summary: On a Starbase tour, Musk argues manufacturing is vastly underrated and design overrated, then lays out his five-step process: make requirements less dumb, delete, simplify, accelerate, automate. He illustrates it with Falcon 1, Model 3 battery mats, Starship grid fins and thrusters.

principles.text: Manufacturing is underrated and design is overrated; the production system takes far more effort than the product itself.
principles.quote: manufacturing is underrated and design is overrated

principles.text: Make requirements less dumb, and tie every requirement to a named person, not a department, who takes responsibility for it.
principles.quote: whatever requirement or constraint you have it must come with a name not a department because you can't ask their apartment you have to ask a person

principles.text: Delete the part or process step first. If you aren't adding things back at least 10% of the time, you aren't deleting enough.
principles.quote: if you're not adding things back in ten per time you're clearly not deleting enough

principles.text: Don't optimize something that shouldn't exist; the most common error of a smart engineer is optimizing the thing that should not exist.
principles.quote: possibly the most common error of a smart engineer is to optimize the thing that should not exist

principles.text: Order matters: question requirements, delete, simplify, then accelerate cycle time, and only then automate.
principles.quote: accelerate cycle time you're moving too slowly go faster but don't go faster until you have worked on the other three things first

principles.text: Remove in-process testing once problems are diagnosed; it chokes cycle time and rejects good parts. Test mostly at end of line.
principles.quote: you just really want to move things pretty much almost always to just test at the end line that's it
